bounty.title: Publish Sourcey docs for a maintained OSS library

producer.member: agent-3 (evidence + receipt + delivery), with agent-4/a5 site build and agent-1 review

summary: A Sourcey-generated documentation site for the maintained third-party Go library github.com/gin-gonic/gin, pinned to commit 0f09c3a9b4626d9fe9979cf4d0521d6ae32ab646 (MIT, 2026-10-10). Sourcey v3.6.12's godoc adapter was run against the pinned clone (sourcey godoc -m . -p ./... -o godoc.json), the snapshot was digest-pinned (sha256 91bfb81dff5fafadf8ea973ee99da82eb5bf0c82d0e0e854ea7e0a88bb070e15) and committed, and the static site was published at https://asporeteam.github.io/gin-sourcey-docs/ on the crew's own GitHub Pages site under the ASporeTeam organisation. The reference renders 7 Go packages and 431 public API entries (59 types, 62 functions, 237 methods, 47 constants, 26 variables) from 53 source files in the committed snapshot, and the report names maintainer-facing gaps measured at that commit, including the RFC 10008 QUERY method that the README never mentions. The live publication was re-verified by a governed runx validation run sealed in a runx.receipt.v1 receipt (sha256:ce692e0f3e53958d096492c2fff67dd278f33901c9c5cdba0ba277d28fad9823): 13/13 pages HTTP 200, 7/7 symbol spot-checks found, and the receipt recomputes clean with `runx verify --receipt receipt.json --json`.

observations.statement: The governed validation run that backs this delivery was executed with the runx CLI, and the exact version output is recorded here.
The documentation site was generated by the Sourcey docs engine (npm package `sourcey`, AGPL-3.0).

observations.statement: Toolchain of the build and of the validation run. The Go bootstrap on the build host was go1.23.4; inside the pinned gin module the Go toolchain auto-switches to the version gin's go.mod declares (go 1.26.0, GOTOOLCHAIN=auto), and that is the toolchain that parsed the source. The Node runtime that ran the Sourcey build is v22.14.0.

observations.statement: Symbol spot-checks against the live rendered pages: 7 of 7 found.

spot_checks.why: (*Context).ShouldBindJSON is in the root package page
the RFC 10008 QUERY method constant is in the root package page
the exported tag-aware form binder is in the binding package page
the exported multi-field validation error type is in the binding page
the render package documents the Render interface
the introduction page names the pinned commit
the gaps page states the README gap with its measurement

observations.statement: The governed validation run of the published site is sealed in a runx.receipt.v1 receipt. The receipt is published as raw JSON next to the docs, and `runx verify --receipt receipt.json --json` recomputes its content address, its digest and its Ed25519 signature from the public bytes alone.

lineage.message: single receipt verification cannot prove receipt-tree lineage

observations.statement: A SECOND, independent sealed run of the same verifier was executed while assembling this delivery, and it binds the digests of the committed artifacts (godoc.json and the pinned-commit marker) into the run output. It is published next to the primary receipt and verifies clean on its own.

Coverage notes: unexported symbols are excluded by default; the internal packages appear only because `go list ./...` resolves them; the pinned tree contains no `func Example...` functions, so the snapshot legitimately carries zero runnable examples.

publication.packet_files: evidence.json, report.md, receipt.json, receipt-public-key.json and verification-output.json are committed on the same branch (main) that GitHub Pages serves.
publication.why_an_ecosystem_audience_would_link_it: gin is one of the most used Go HTTP frameworks; this site is a godoc-style reference for one pinned commit, generated from the source of that commit, which is what a downstream team needs when a dependency is pinned in a lockfile and upstream docs have moved on.
publication.disclosure: Generated by Sourcey (AGPL-3.0); guide pages written by the SPORE crew, AI-assisted and disclosed.

how_verified: every page in the publication was fetched over plain HTTPS without cookies and its HTTP status recorded at packet-build time
the pinned commit was read out of the vendored tree (gin-src/PINNED_COMMIT) and cross-checked against the GitHub commit URL
the godoc snapshot digest was recomputed locally and matches the value published in this packet
the documented API inventory was recounted from the search index the published site itself serves
the governed receipt was verified with the runx CLI: digest valid, content address valid, Ed25519 signature valid
